body:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Go/No-Go approval request: Provision-to-ready staged rollout (us-east / A100 only) — Oct 10 window

Priya, Sean — requesting go/no-go approval to enable the first staged rollout of the provision-to-ready automation in prod.

Scope of rollout (tight blast radius)
- Region/GPU: us-east / A100 only
- Pools: Dedicated new capacity + expansion nodes only (no impact to existing serving nodes unless they are reimaged/reprovisioned)
- Feature flag: fleet.provisioning.staged_rollout_enabled = true for (region=us-east, sku=a100)
- Image channel: candidate -> stable promotion remains manual for this stage; we are only changing the provisioning workflow + validations + readiness gating.

Proposed window
- Fri Oct 10, 10:00–12:00 PT (with Infra + SRE on bridge if needed)

Success criteria (stop/go)
- Time-to-ready P95 for newly allocated nodes <= 45 min over the window
- Provision-to-ready success rate >= 97% (no more than 3% of nodes failing validations)
- No paging-alert storm from new metrics/alerts (tickets OK; paging only for hard failures)

Stop conditions (immediate rollback)
- >10 nodes in a 30-min window stuck in Provisioning or Validating > 60 min
- Validation failure rate > 8% sustained for 30 min (excluding known pre-existing hardware failures)
- Any evidence of readiness gate preventing nodes from joining serving pools erroneously

Risk assessment (summary)
- Primary risk: validation flakes (NCCL smoke) causing quarantine spikes -> capacity shortfall.
  - Mitigation: quarantine threshold set to N=2 failures before quarantine; auto-retry with backoff; operator override remains available.
- Secondary risk: metric tag/cardinality issues during early rollout.
  - Mitigation: per-node identifiers removed from metric tags; alert rules reviewed by SRE; dashboards validated in staging.
- Control-plane risk: readiness state mismatch / incomplete failure reasons.
  - Mitigation: readiness service writes are idempotent; fallback to Quarantined state when artifacts are missing; audit events on image channel changes are enabled.

Roll-back plan (fast)
1) Disable staged rollout flag for us-east/a100 (takes effect within ~2–5 minutes)
2) Revert to previous provisioning path (legacy join + manual checks)
3) For nodes mid-flight: mark as Quarantined (not Ready) until operator triage; no nodes will be admitted to serving pool without passing readiness gate
4) If we see image-related failures: pin pool image channel to last-known stable (no candidate promotion)

Attachments
- us-east-a100-staged-rollout-checklist-v1.3.pdf
- risk-assessment-us-east-a100-staged-rollout-v0.9.docx
- rollback-plan-provision-to-ready-us-east-a100-v1.1.md

If you approve, Irene is CC’d for exec visibility and we’ll send the final “go” note to Infra/SRE on-call + release channel with the window and links.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Engineering Manager, Infra/Fleet
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Go/No-Go approval request: Provision-to-ready staged rollout (us-east / A100 only) — Oct 10 window

A few SRE questions before I sign off:

1) Paging vs ticketing: which alerts are paging during the window? I want us to avoid “new alert” pages unless it’s actually customer-impacting.
2) What’s the exact definition of “allocated” and “ready” for the SLI you’re referencing? (We’ve had confusion here in past rollouts.)
3) If quarantine spikes, who owns the decision to lower thresholds vs rollback? I prefer rollback over threshold-tuning in the first window.

If you can answer those, I’m OK with the controlled blast radius.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 10:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: Go/No-Go approval request: Provision-to-ready staged rollout (us-east / A100 only) — Oct 10 window

Sean — answers inline.

1) Paging vs ticketing
- Paging (during window only):
  - Provision-to-ready hard failure rate > 8% for 30m (us-east/a100)
  - Readiness service write failures (5xx) > 2% for 10m
  - “Nodes stuck in Validating” > 10 nodes for > 60m
- Ticket-only:
  - Step-level flake rate warnings (NCCL retries, disk warmup taking longer)
  - Increased P95 without crossing stop threshold

2) SLI definitions
- “Allocated” timestamp: capacity system emits NodeAllocated event when instance is assigned to a pool (this is the first timestamp we can reliably fetch across AWS + our fleet DB).
- “Ready” timestamp: readiness service writes state=Ready after post-flight validations pass AND the readiness gate allows the node to join the serving pool.
- We’re explicitly not using “kubelet joined” as Ready.

3) Quarantine spike decision owner
- Agree: rollback > tuning.
- Decision owner during window: me (Infra) in consultation with on-call SRE lead (designated for the window). If quarantine spikes past stop conditions, we rollback the feature flag.
- We won’t change thresholds live without your OK; tuning can happen post-window with ENG-4830 follow-ups.

We’ll also have a standing bridge with a single point of contact on both teams.

Vanessa

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 11:12 AM PT
Subject: Re: Go/No-Go approval request: Provision-to-ready staged rollout (us-east / A100 only) — Oct 10 window

Thanks. Two platform/control-plane checks from my side:

- Can you confirm the readiness service is the single source of truth for the Ready/Quarantined state (not fleet agent local state)?
- For rollback, is there any scenario where nodes could be admitted to serving pools without passing the readiness gate? (I’m OK with us being conservative and leaving nodes out, but not the reverse.)

If both are “yes / no” respectively, I’m comfortable approving.

Priya Natarajan
VP Engineering, Platform Control Plane
Redwood Inference


---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 11:37 AM PT
Subject: Re: Go/No-Go approval request: Provision-to-ready staged rollout (us-east / A100 only) — Oct 10 window

Priya — confirmed.

- Source of truth: readiness service is authoritative for current state. The agent heartbeat/validation results are inputs; the control-plane write is what determines Ready vs Quarantined.
- Admission safety: no scenario where nodes are admitted without passing the readiness gate. The serving pool admission controller now checks readiness state=Ready (PR-18496). If the flag is rolled back, admission remains gated; we simply revert to the legacy provisioning workflow for bringing nodes up to “joined cluster,” but the Ready gate still holds.

Net effect of rollback is “more manual + slower” but safe.

Vanessa

Thanks for keeping the blast radius tight.

Irene Choi
